## Function Emit Document

One JSON document + newline on stdout; --pretty indents by 2.

Behaviour: renderDocument(doc, pretty) = JSON.stringify(doc, null, 2 when pretty) + "\n". errorDocument(code, kind, message) = {error: {code, kind, message}}, keys in that order. main writes exactly one rendered document to stdout per invocation and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.

Steps:
- produces: Error Document

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given doc {a: 1, b: [true, null]}, pretty false; when rendered; then "{\"a\":1,\"b\":[true,null]}\n"
2. given the same doc, pretty true; when rendered; then "{\n \"a\": 1,\n \"b\": [\n true,\n null\n ]\n}\n"
3. given errorDocument(4, "UsageError", "unknown command: x"); when rendered compact; then "{\"error\":{\"code\":4,\"kind\":\"UsageError\",\"message\":\"unknown command: x\"}}\n"

Data Error Document: The document of every non-result exit.
Schema:
{ error: { code: 0|1|2|3|4, kind: 'UsageError'|'NotYetError'|'DeckError'|'RefusalError'|'RuntimeError', message: string } }

Module: `src/cli/types.ts`; test: `src/cli/document.ts`.

## Function Classify Error

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 a run with any card not written; 2 a refusal before any spend (invalid deck, hazard errors, dirty tree, existing branch); 3 a fault thrown once a command is under way (a failing git command, an archive not committed, I/O); 4 a usage error (bad flag, unknown or not-yet command, missing file, unconfigured processor). Error document {"error": {"code", "kind", "message"}}.

Behaviour: classifyThrown(e) → {code: 3, document: errorDocument(3, "RuntimeError", e's message when e is an Error, else String(e))}. runExitCode(report, archive) → 3 when the archive is not ok; else 1 when any outcome's status is not "written"; else 0. Kinds: UsageError and NotYetError (4), DeckError and RefusalError (2), RuntimeError (3).

Steps:
- produces: Command Result

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given new Error("git add failed (exit 1): fatal: x"); when classifyThrown; then {code: 3, document: {error: {code: 3, kind: "RuntimeError", message: "git add failed (exit 1): fatal: x"}}}
2. given the string "boom"; when classifyThrown; then {code: 3, document: {error: {code: 3, kind: "RuntimeError", message: "boom"}}}
3. given reports with outcomes [written, written] and [written, skipped], archive ok; then [written] with archive {ok: false}; when runExitCode; then 0, 1, 3

Data Command Result: What a command returns to main.
Schema:
{ code: 0|1|2|3|4, document: unknown }

Module: `src/cli/types.ts`; test: `src/cli/document.ts`.

## Function Read Deck File

The deck file a command names, resolved against the root, loaded by Load Deck.

Behaviour: readDeckFile(root, deckPath): abs = path.resolve(root, deckPath) (an absolute deckPath ignores root). Not a regular file → {ok: false, result: {code: 4, document: errorDocument(4, "UsageError", "deck file not found: <deckPath as given>")}}. Else Load Deck on its UTF-8 text; faults → {ok: false, result: {code: 2, document: errorDocument(2, "DeckError", "invalid deck: " + each fault as "<key>: <message>" joined by "; ")}}. Else {ok: true, deck}.

Steps:
- reads: Deck
- produces: Command Result

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given a tmp root with d.json = the deck of the tiny fixture; when readDeckFile(root, "d.json"); then {ok: true, deck: {cards: [card a with every default filled], externalDependsOn: []}} (ref: tests/fixtures/decks/tiny.json (one card a → src/a.ts))

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.

## Function Deck Check

`morph deck check`: generations, hazards and slice weights of a deck file; exit 2 on any error hazard.

Behaviour: deckCheckCommand(root, deckPath, sliceCapBytes): Read Deck File (its failure is the result); weighing = Weigh Slices(deck, root, sliceCapBytes); hazards = Find Hazards(deck) followed by the weighing's hazards; document {deck: deckPath as given, cards: the card count, generations: Layer Generations(deck), errors and warnings: the hazards of severity error / warning counted, hazards, weights: the weighing's weights}, keys in that order; code 2 when errors > 0, else 0.

Steps:
- calls: Read Deck File
- uses: cards
- produces: Deck Check Document

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given a tmp root holding only d.json = the write-write fixture (a and b both write src/x.ts); when deckCheckCommand(root, "d.json", 500000); then code 2; document {deck: "d.json", cards: 2, generations: [["a", "b"]], errors: 1, warnings: 0, hazards: [{kind: "write-write", severity: "error", cards: ["a", "b"], path: "src/x.ts", repair: null}], weights: [{card: "a", bytes: 0, missing: ["docs/a.md", "src/x.ts"]}, {card: "b", bytes: 0, missing: ["docs/b.md", "src/x.ts"]}]} (ref: tests/fixtures/decks/hazardsWriteWrite.json)
2. given d.json = the tiny fixture and src/a.ts = "export const a = 1;\n" (20 bytes); when deckCheckCommand(root, "d.json", 500000); then code 0; errors 0, warnings 1, hazards [{kind: "implicit-read", severity: "warning", cards: ["a"], path: null, repair: null}], weights [{card: "a", bytes: 20, missing: []}] (ref: tests/fixtures/decks/tiny.json)
3. given the same tree, sliceCapBytes 10; when checked; then code 0; warnings 2; hazards [the implicit-read, then {kind: "oversized-slice", severity: "warning", cards: ["a"], path: null, repair: null, bytes: 20, cap: 10}]

Data Deck Check Document: stdout of deck check.
Schema:
{ deck: string, cards: number, generations: string[][], errors: number, warnings: number, hazards: Hazard[], weights: SliceWeight[] }

## Function Parse Command

argv into one Command or a usage error; global --root and --pretty anywhere.

Behaviour: parseCommand(argv) scans argv left to right. A token starting with "--" is a flag: --pretty takes no value; --root, --deck, --processor, --run-id, --deadline, --max-cards, --max-retry-batches, --slice-cap-bytes take the next token whatever it is; any other flag (also --x=y) → "unknown flag: <t>"; a value flag as the last token → "flag <t> needs a value"; a flag seen twice → "flag <t> given twice" (the first such error in argv order wins). Every other token is a word. Then the command from the words: none → "no command (commands: deck check, run)"; "run" → run; "deck" "check" → deck check; a first word plan, scout, primer, review or report → NotYetError "command <word> is not available yet"; "deck" followed by add, status, reset or clear → NotYetError "command deck <w> is not available yet"; anything else → "unknown command: <words joined by a space>". More words than the command takes → "unexpected argument: <first extra>". Then, in this order: a flag the command does not take → "flag <f> does not apply to <command>" (deck check takes --root, --pretty, --deck, --slice-cap-bytes; run takes --root, --pretty, --deck, --processor, --run-id, --deadline, --max-cards, --max-retry-batches), in argv order; no --deck → "missing --deck"; run without --processor → "missing --processor"; for run a --run-id not matching ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ → "--run-id must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ (got '<v>')"; numbers in the order --slice-cap-bytes (deck check), --deadline, --max-cards, --max-retry-batches (run): digits only, ≥ 1 ("<f> must be a positive integer (got '<v>')"), --max-retry-batches ≥ 0 ("must be a non-negative integer"). Every failure is {ok: false, error: {error: {code: 4, kind: "UsageError" | "NotYetError", message}}}. Defaults: root ".", pretty false, sliceCapBytes 500000, runId null, deadlineSeconds 2400, maxCards null (= the deck's card count), maxRetryBatches 2.

Steps:
- produces: Command

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given argv ["deck", "check", "--deck", "d.json"]; when parsed; then {ok: true, command: {name: "deck check", root: ".", pretty: false, deck: "d.json", sliceCapBytes: 500000}}
2. given argv ["--pretty", "run", "--deck", "d.json", "--processor", "s", "--root", "/r", "--run-id", "r1", "--deadline", "60", "--max-cards", "3", "--max-retry-batches", "0"]; when parsed; then {ok: true, command: {name: "run", root: "/r", pretty: true, deck: "d.json", processor: "s", runId: "r1", deadlineSeconds: 60, maxCards: 3, maxRetryBatches: 0}}
3. given argv ["frobnicate"]; when parsed; then {ok: false, error: {error: {code: 4, kind: "UsageError", message: "unknown command: frobnicate"}}}
4. given argv ["plan"], then ["deck", "status"]; when parsed; then NotYetError (code 4) "command plan is not available yet", then NotYetError "command deck status is not available yet"
5. given argv ["run", "--deck", "d.json"]; when parsed; then UsageError "missing --processor"
6. given argv ["deck", "check", "--deck", "d.json", "--processor", "s"]; when parsed; then UsageError "flag --processor does not apply to deck check"
7. given argv ["run", "--deck", "d", "--processor", "s", "--deadline", "0"]; when parsed; then UsageError "--deadline must be a positive integer (got '0')"
8. given argv ["--root"], then []; when parsed; then UsageError "flag --root needs a value", then UsageError "no command (commands: deck check, run)"

Data Command: One parsed invocation.
Schema:
{ name: 'deck check', root, pretty, deck, sliceCapBytes } | { name: 'run', root, pretty, deck, processor, runId: string | null, deadlineSeconds, maxCards: number | null, maxRetryBatches }

## Function Run Command

`morph run`: processor, deck, hazards, run branch, Run Deck with git's commit hook, archive; one Run Document.

Behaviour: runCommand(root, args, deps), every check before any git call or spend, in this order. 1. readRegistry(deps.env); no config with id args.processor → code 4 UsageError "processor <id> is not configured", plus ": " and the messages of the registry faults whose key starts with "MORPH_PROCESSOR_<id>_" joined by "; " when there are any. 2. Read Deck File (its failure is the result). 3. Find Hazards errors → code 2 RefusalError "deck has <n> hazard error(s): " + each as "<kind> <cards joined by ",">[ <path>]" joined by "; ". 4. start = deps.now() (the only call of runCommand itself); runId = args.runId, or mintRunId(start) = the UTC time of start as "YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS". 5. Open Run Branch(root, runId, deps.env); a refusal → code 2 RefusalError with its error. 6. Run Deck with input {root, runId, branch, deck, budget {maxCards: args.maxCards or the card count, maxRetryBatches, deadline: start + deadlineSeconds × 1000}} and deps {config, transport: deps.transport or realTransport(config.timeoutMs), commit: makeCommitHook(root, config.model, deps.env), now: deps.now, env: deps.env}. 7. Archive Run(root, {runId, deck, report}, deps.env). → {code: runExitCode(report, archive), document: {runId, branch, base, report, archive}}. A thrown Error (a git command failing, I/O) propagates to main. The checkout stays on the run branch.

Steps:
- uses: processor
- calls: Read Deck File
- uses: git
- uses: runloop
- produces: Run Document
